# Land Quotient

> Land Quotient is a parcel map and site-selection tool for commercial real estate: every assessor parcel in a county on one map, with zoning, FEMA flood zones, building footprints and owner portfolios on each lot, and plain-English questions answered across the whole county.

Land Quotient is built for commercial brokers, developers, investment-sales teams and investors who need to find sites and owners quickly. It is a free web app (an account is required) at https://landquotient.com.

## What it does

- Every parcel in a county on one map, with the county's own assessment record: owner of record, assessed value, land use, lot size.
- Zoning districts and FEMA flood hazard areas on each parcel, usable as county-wide filters ("outside the flood zone, zoned anything but residential").
- Building footprints on each lot: how many buildings, footprint and share of the lot covered, so vacant and under-built sites can be found.
- Owner portfolios: one holder across its many entity names and mailing addresses.
- Site feasibility: a screen of any lot for slope, FEMA flood hazard, wetlands and protected land, with the acres that pass; a site search can be screened and ranked in one step.
- Building permits, submitted and approved plans and code cases on the map and on each lot, where the city publishes them.
- Pieces for a brief: maps and tables (feasibility, property record, demographics, nearby retail) to copy into the user's own branded document.
- Ask: type a question in plain English, see the matching parcels highlighted, open them as a table and export a list.
- Live ship positions for coastal markets, permits, traffic counts and census overlays where published.

## Markets

More than 100 markets in 29 states are live as of November 2026, among them Austin, Houston, Dallas, Phoenix, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, San Diego, Orange County, New York City, North Jersey, Chicago, Philadelphia, Boston, Washington DC, Miami-Dade, Broward, Tampa, Nashville, Denver, Detroit and Minneapolis. A market is usually one county. The current list, with parcel counts and what each market publishes, is at https://landquotient.com/markets and is the source to quote: new markets are added most months.

## Connect an AI assistant

Land Quotient has a Model Context Protocol (MCP) connector at https://landquotient.com/mcp (streamable HTTP, OAuth sign-in with a free Land Quotient account, no API key). An assistant that connects can search parcels, read one parcel in full, screen a lot for slope, flood hazard, wetlands and protected land, list the chains and landmarks around a site, and save maps. It exposes two tools, search and execute; https://landquotient.com/mcp/classic lists one tool per operation instead. Directions: https://landquotient.com/connect

## Data

Parcel records come from each county's published assessment roll; zoning from city and county GIS; flood zones from FEMA's National Flood Hazard Layer; building footprints from Overture Maps (OpenStreetMap contributors and others, ODbL). Parcel-level data is available to signed-in subscribers in the app; it is not offered as a bulk download.
